items.title: Discrimination-Insensitive Pricing via KL-Divergence Optimization
items.source_summary: The paper proposes a framework for fair financial pricing that eliminates sensitivity to protected covariates (e.g., gender, ethnicity) by finding the nearest probability measure to the real-world distribution under KL-divergence that satisfies a discrimination-insensitivity constraint. The approach is formulated as a constrained optimization problem with regulatory and ethical motivations.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: This work addresses ethical/regulatory pricing fairness in insurance and credit products. SOFAR's pipeline focuses on market signal generation, options flow, GEX, and AI-driven trade scoring — none of which involve demographic-covariate pricing or fair lending constraints. There is no meaningful mapping to any SOFAR component.
items.evidence_basis: No connection to SOFAR's signal generation, scoring, or risk management components
items.credibility_basis: Peer-reviewed arXiv preprint with formal mathematical framework; no empirical backtest against market data
items.author: Kathleen Miao, Silvana Pesenti

items.title: LLM-to-Options Strategy via Domain-Specific Query Language (OQL)
items.source_summary: The paper introduces OQL (Option Query Language), a domain-specific intermediate representation that allows LLMs to translate natural-language trading intents into executable options strategies reliably. By abstracting multi-dimensional option chain data into grammatical primitives, OQL acts as a semantic parser layer that avoids the pitfalls of free-form code generation, enabling deterministic strategy instantiation.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's AI synthesis layer (likely ai_synthesis.py or equivalent LLM orchestration module) currently translates macro/options signals into trade recommendations in natural language or semi-structured outputs. There is no evidence of a structured intermediate representation (DSL) enforcing options-specific constraints (strike selection, expiry, spread construction) before strategy output. This means the AI layer may produce semantically valid but operationally invalid or unconstrained options recommendations. Introducing an OQL-style intermediate layer between the AI scoring output and the final trade recommendation formatter could enforce grammatical correctness and constraint satisfaction on multi-leg options structures.

proposed_change.target_component: ai_synthesis.py (or equivalent LLM orchestration/trade recommendation module)
proposed_change.change_description: Design and integrate a lightweight Option Query Language (OQL) intermediate representation layer between the AI synthesis output and the trade recommendation formatter. Define a grammar covering key option primitives (underlying, expiry, strike, right, quantity, spread type). Have the LLM output OQL-structured queries rather than free-form text; validate and parse them deterministically before rendering final trade cards. This reduces hallucinated or constraint-violating strategy outputs.

items.evidence_basis: Paper provides concrete architectural solution with demonstrated reduction in strategy generation errors; directly applicable to SOFAR's LLM-based recommendation pipeline
items.credibility_basis: arXiv preprint with system design and evaluation; no independent replication yet
items.author: Haochen Luo, Zhengzhao Lai, Junjie Xu, Yifan Li, Tang Pok Hin, Yuan Zhang, Chen Liu

items.title: MEV Auction Format Analysis on Ethereum Blockchain Markets
items.source_summary: Using 2.2 million Ethereum transactions, the paper finds that MEV extracted values follow a log-normal distribution with extreme right-tail concentration, competition intensity varies by MEV type, and the Revenue Equivalence Theorem breaks down due to correlated searcher valuations. The authors model this via a Gaussian common factor and derive equilibrium bidding strategies across five auction formats.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: This research is specific to on-chain MEV dynamics and blockchain auction mechanism design. SOFAR's pipeline targets traditional equity and options markets (GEX, VIX, options flow, macro signals). Crypto-specific MEV mechanics do not map to any current SOFAR component — not GEX, not VIX term structure, not sentiment analysis, and not macro event modeling.
items.evidence_basis: Domain mismatch: blockchain MEV vs. equity/options market focus of SOFAR
items.credibility_basis: Large empirical dataset (2.2M transactions), formal equilibrium modeling, well-defined methodology
items.author: Aleksei Adadurov, Sergey Barseghyan, Anton Chtepine, Antero Eloranta, Andrei Sebyakin, Arsenii Valitov

items.title: Short-Horizon Duesenberry Equilibrium with Heterogeneous Preferences
items.source_summary: The paper develops a continuous-time general equilibrium model where a heterogeneous population repeatedly optimizes over short horizons using relative-income (Duesenberry-type) utility. The model uses Brownian flows on a type space to capture time-varying preferences driven by demographic change and social shifts, establishing existence of equilibrium and characterizing asset price dynamics.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: This is a theoretical macro-finance equilibrium paper focused on preference heterogeneity and demographic-driven utility shifts. While tangentially related to macro modeling, it does not provide actionable signal improvements for SOFAR's event tree, sentiment analysis, or any other pipeline component. The abstraction level is too high and empirically ungrounded for near-term integration.
items.evidence_basis: Purely theoretical framework with no empirical validation or tradeable signal implications
items.credibility_basis: Formal mathematical proofs presented; no empirical data or market backtest
items.author: Jaime Alberto Londoño

items.title: Heterogeneous Returns Break Wealth Tax Neutrality in Fokker-Planck Models
items.source_summary: The paper extends a Fokker-Planck framework to populations with heterogeneous, persistent return-generating ability, showing that a proportional wealth tax ceases to be economically neutral when investor drift coefficients vary. The analysis derives consequences for the stationary wealth distribution, asset prices, and portfolio allocations across ability types.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: This is a theoretical public finance and wealth distribution paper with no direct application to SOFAR's signal pipeline. The Fokker-Planck modeling of wealth dynamics under tax policy does not connect to GEX calculation, options flow detection, VIX term structure, or AI synthesis components.
items.evidence_basis: No empirical signal or market microstructure content; purely theoretical tax incidence analysis
items.credibility_basis: Builds on prior published framework; formal derivations provided with no empirical test
items.author: Anders G Frøseth

items.title: Portfolio Neutrality Under Multiple Ownership Tax Structures
items.source_summary: The paper generalizes a prior result showing that proportional wealth taxes preserve portfolio neutrality by examining the full system of shareholder taxes — corporate, capital income, dividend/capital gains, and wealth taxes. Each tax type modifies the drift of the wealth process differently (multiplicative, constant shift, or regime-dependent compression) while leaving diffusion unchanged, and the combined system is shown to preserve portfolio neutrality under specific conditions.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: This is a theoretical public finance paper on portfolio neutrality under various tax regimes. While it touches on portfolio choice, it does not provide novel market signals, improve options flow detection, enhance GEX calculation, or contribute to SOFAR's AI scoring methodology. Tax neutrality proofs are not actionable for a real-time trading signal pipeline.
items.evidence_basis: Purely theoretical; no market data, no tradeable signal, no connection to SOFAR pipeline components
items.credibility_basis: Rigorous mathematical framework; companion paper to lab-0004 by same author
items.author: Anders G Frøseth

items.title: Optimal Auto-Deleveraging via Leverage-Minimizing Position Reduction
items.source_summary: The paper formalizes Auto-Deleveraging (ADL) on crypto futures exchanges as a risk-minimization optimization problem, showing that under a risk-neutral expected loss objective the optimal policy uniquely minimizes maximum leverage among participants. The resulting mechanism provides a transparent, rank-based protocol for socialized loss absorption during extreme price moves.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's risk management component likely tracks position sizing and stop-loss logic but may not model counterparty/exchange-level deleveraging cascades that can amplify price moves in crypto or highly leveraged equity futures markets. When large forced liquidations or ADL events occur, they create detectable options flow anomalies and delta-hedging demand spikes that SOFAR's GEX calculator and options flow detector could benefit from recognizing as a distinct signal regime. Specifically, gex_calculator.py and options_flow_detector.py do not appear to incorporate leverage-concentration metrics as a conditioning variable for signal strength. Additionally, risk_management.py could incorporate an ADL-inspired maximum-leverage monitoring signal to flag when market-wide leverage concentration reaches levels historically associated with cascade liquidations.

proposed_change.change_description: Implement a leverage-concentration monitoring module inspired by the ADL framework: (1) In risk_management.py, add a market-wide open interest weighted average leverage proxy (using futures OI and price data) that flags regime shifts when leverage concentration exceeds a rolling percentile threshold. (2) In gex_calculator.py, condition GEX signal strength on the leverage regime flag — elevated leverage concentration should amplify GEX-driven flow estimates since forced unwinds accelerate delta-hedging demand. Start with crypto futures (BTC, ETH) as the initial test asset class given data availability.

items.evidence_basis: Formal optimization framework with clear structural results; indirect applicability to SOFAR via leverage-cascade signal logic rather than direct implementation of ADL protocol
items.credibility_basis: Published by researchers at Columbia (Moallemi) and NYU (Nutz), rigorous optimization proof with practical exchange design implications
items.author: Steven Campbell, Natascha Hey, Ciamac C. Moallemi, Marcel Nutz

items.title: HAMD: Native Cubic Portfolio Optimization Avoiding Quadratization Distortion
items.source_summary: The paper proposes Hyper-Adaptive Momentum Dynamics (HAMD), a hybrid optimization method that operates natively on cubic cardinality-constrained portfolio objectives without requiring Rosenberg quadratization, which inflates variable count from n to 5n and distorts the search landscape. HAMD combines continuous Hamiltonian dynamics with adaptive momentum to solve higher-order Markowitz-style problems incorporating three-way sector co-movement terms.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's AI scoring and portfolio construction methodology likely relies on standard quadratic mean-variance optimization or linear factor models for position sizing and signal aggregation. If SOFAR's scoring model (ai_synthesis.py or portfolio_optimizer.py) attempts to capture three-way interactions between sector rotations, macro regimes, and volatility signals — which is plausible given multi-signal synthesis — it may be implicitly flattening higher-order interactions into quadratic approximations, losing information. The HAMD approach suggests that incorporating cubic co-movement terms (e.g., sector × macro_regime × vol_regime) without quadratization could improve signal aggregation fidelity. This is particularly relevant for SOFAR's multi-factor AI synthesis where cross-signal interactions are likely non-quadratic. However, the paper is a preprint with no comparative empirical validation on real portfolio data, reducing confidence.

proposed_change.change_description: Investigate whether the current signal aggregation/scoring objective function captures only pairwise (quadratic) signal interactions or higher-order terms. If quadratic, prototype a cubic extension incorporating three-way interaction terms between: (1) GEX regime, (2) VIX term structure slope, and (3) sector momentum. Implement HAMD or a simpler native cubic solver (e.g., gradient descent on the cubic objective without quadratization) on a small n signal set. Backtest against current quadratic baseline using SOFAR's prediction backcheck framework to measure incremental accuracy.

items.evidence_basis: Theoretically motivated but no published empirical validation on real financial data; methodology is novel but unproven at scale
items.credibility_basis: Single-author preprint with no peer review, no empirical results on real portfolio data, no comparison baseline performance metrics disclosed
items.author: Greg Serbarinov

items.title: Telematics Risk Index via Wavelet + Frequency-Severity Joint Model
items.source_summary: The paper proposes a trip-level risk index combining frequency of abnormal driving events with a severity component benchmarked against portfolio-level baselines using inverse-probability penalties for tail extremes. High-frequency telematics signals are decomposed via maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform (MODWT) to capture multi-scale patterns. The framework jointly models frequency and severity for driver/trip risk scoring.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: This research addresses insurance telematics and actuarial risk scoring for individual drivers using IoT sensor data. It has no meaningful connection to SOFAR's financial market pipeline — no options flow, GEX, VIX, macro signals, or equity/derivatives data involved. The wavelet decomposition concept is interesting but is applied in a non-market context with no transferable methodology for SOFAR's current signal stack.
items.evidence_basis: Domain mismatch: telematics/insurance actuarial science vs. financial market prediction pipeline
items.credibility_basis: Peer-reviewed arXiv preprint from credentialed actuarial science authors (Badescu, Lin are well-known in actuarial literature)
items.author: Jongtaek Lee, Andrei Badescu, X. Sheldon Lin

items.title: Robust Worst-Case Liquidation Strategy Under Price Impact
items.source_summary: The paper models optimal early asset liquidation in financial crises, where fire-sale dynamics cause price impact when large illiquid positions are unwound simultaneously. A two-period model is introduced allowing pre-clearing liquidation to reduce clearing-time price impact, solved via a worst-case robust optimization framework. The approach maximizes the minimum liquid asset value across adversarial scenarios.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's risk management layer likely lacks a formal price-impact-aware position unwinding model. When SOFAR generates directional trade setups or monitors institutional flow signals, it does not appear to account for adverse liquidation dynamics under stress — particularly relevant for large-cap options positions or concentrated GEX exposures during volatility spikes. The robust worst-case framing could improve SOFAR's risk_management module (likely risk_manager.py or position_sizing.py) by adding a liquidation cost penalty term when scoring high-conviction trades near expiration or during elevated VIX regimes. This is especially pertinent when GEX flips negative and delta-hedging flows become destabilizing.

proposed_change.target_component: risk_manager.py (or equivalent position sizing/exit logic module)
proposed_change.change_description: Add a worst-case liquidation cost adjustment to position exit scoring. When GEX is negative and VIX term structure is inverted (stress regime), apply a price-impact penalty to expected P&L of large open positions, scaling discount with position size relative to estimated ADV. Implement a two-stage exit check: (1) pre-stress voluntary early exit scoring and (2) forced liquidation cost estimate at clearing, mirroring the paper's two-period structure.

items.evidence_basis: Theoretically rigorous model with direct application to institutional risk management; however, no empirical backtesting results on real market data are provided in the abstract
items.credibility_basis: arXiv preprint with formal mathematical framework; authors appear affiliated with academic finance/math programs
items.author: Dohyun Ahn, Hongyi Jiang

items.title: Multi-Dimensional LLM Sentiment (Relevance, Polarity, Intensity, Uncertainty, Forwardness) for Crude Oil Futures
items.source_summary: This paper moves beyond simple positive/negative polarity by extracting five sentiment dimensions from energy news using GPT-4o and Llama 3.2: relevance, polarity, intensity, uncertainty, and forwardness (forward-looking tone). Weekly WTI crude oil futures returns from 2020–2025 are used as the prediction target, with LLM-derived signals benchmarked against FinBERT and AlphaVantage. Results suggest multi-dimensional signals improve predictive power over polarity-only baselines.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: SOFAR's sentiment analysis component (likely sentiment_analyzer.py or news_processor.py) almost certainly relies on polarity-dominant scoring — a well-known limitation. This paper directly demonstrates that decomposing sentiment into uncertainty and forwardness dimensions adds predictive signal beyond polarity, which is immediately applicable to SOFAR's AI synthesis layer. Specifically: (1) SOFAR's macro/commodity signal module for energy-sector tickers (USO, XLE, WTI futures) lacks uncertainty and forward-looking tone dimensions; (2) the AI scoring methodology (ai_scorer.py or synthesis_engine.py) could weight news items differently based on relevance scores rather than treating all news equally; (3) the 'forwardness' dimension maps naturally to SOFAR's event tree modeling — forward-looking statements in news should receive higher weight in event impact scoring. The 5-year dataset (2020–2025) spanning COVID, energy crisis, and geopolitical shocks provides strong empirical validation.

proposed_change.change_description: Extend the sentiment extraction prompt/pipeline to produce five structured output dimensions per news article: (1) relevance score (0-1, is this article market-moving?), (2) polarity (-1 to 1), (3) intensity (magnitude of sentiment), (4) uncertainty (hedging language, probability qualifiers), (5) forwardness (proportion of forward-looking vs. retrospective language). Aggregate weekly by ticker/sector. In the AI scoring layer, weight signals by relevance score and use uncertainty dimension as a confidence modifier on directional predictions. For energy tickers (USO, XLE, CL futures), pilot this 5-dimension framework using GPT-4o structured outputs before generalizing across all sectors.

items.evidence_basis: Empirical study with 5-year out-of-sample period, multiple LLM benchmarks, and direct return prediction results; methodology is reproducible and the five dimensions are explicitly defined
items.credibility_basis: Rigorous empirical study with multiple model comparisons (GPT-4o, Llama 3.2, FinBERT, AlphaVantage) over a 5-year window including multiple market regimes
items.author: Dehao Dai, Ding Ma, Dou Liu, Kerui Geng, Yiqing Wang

items.title: LLMQuant Quant-Wiki: Open-Source Quantitative Finance Knowledge Base
items.source_summary: LLMQuant's quant-wiki is an open-source bilingual (Chinese/English) repository aimed at democratizing quantitative finance knowledge and closing the information gap between domestic Chinese and international quant communities. It has accumulated over 3,200 GitHub stars and 254 forks, indicating substantial community engagement. The project likely covers quantitative strategies, factor models, and implementation guides.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: While quant-wiki is a high-engagement educational resource, it is a knowledge aggregation repository rather than a novel research contribution. It does not surface a specific identifiable gap in SOFAR's pipeline components — no new signal methodology, model architecture, or empirical finding is described in the available content snippet. The value is encyclopedic rather than cutting-edge. SOFAR's development team could use it as a reference resource, but it does not point to a concrete, actionable improvement in any specific SOFAR script or data file.
items.evidence_basis: No specific methodology, empirical results, or novel algorithm described — content is educational/reference material
items.credibility_basis: High community engagement (3,213 stars) suggests quality curation, but open-source wikis vary in depth and accuracy; no peer review
items.author: LLMQuant

items.title: Claude AI Skills for Indian NSE/BSE F&O and Institutional Flow Analysis
items.source_summary: This GitHub project provides Claude AI-powered skills tailored for Indian equity market participants, covering NSE/BSE stocks, futures and options derivatives, institutional flow tracking (FII/DII), and market breadth indicators. It is a low-engagement repository (7 stars) targeting retail traders in the Indian market. The scope includes F&O derivatives analysis specific to Indian exchanges.
items.sofar_gap_analysis: This repository is focused on Indian market microstructure (NSE/BSE) and retail-oriented AI skill wrapping for Claude. SOFAR's pipeline targets US equity and derivatives markets (SPX, SPY, VIX, US options flow). The F&O institutional flow concepts are not novel relative to SOFAR's existing options flow detection capabilities, and the Indian market structure (Nifty/BankNifty, SEBI regulations, FII/DII categorization) does not transfer to US market pipeline components. Engagement is negligible (7 stars), further reducing signal quality. No gap identified.
items.evidence_basis: Minimal engagement, market-specific to India (non-applicable to SOFAR's US focus), no novel methodology described
items.credibility_basis: Only 7 stars/5 forks; no documentation of backtested results or methodology; retail-focused tool wrapper rather than research contribution
